_comment: A collection, not a program: fluxmethods publishes the estimators of this
package as plain functions, with no pipeline, no configuration and nothing
to invoke. So there is no `runtime` and no dialect here -- there is no
config of its own to read and no binary to run -- and the rows below carry
no `selector`, because a collection has no settings to select a method by.
A row with `ours` and no `run` declares what the collection offers without
saying how to call it -- which is legitimate and, here, deliberate: the
marshalling of each shape is verified by bundling the descriptor and running
the protocol tests, and that is gated on four contracts listed in
.claude/plan/bundle_a_collection_descriptor.md. The four resampling rows were
verified that way before the descriptor was moved here.
Seventeen of the twenty-eight rows now say how to call the method, in two
shapes. `array` is plain arrays in and one array back: the four resampling
rows, and they are the only estimators here shaped that way. `dataset:` --
the input role oneflux_preproc added in a717c34 -- hands the period over as
it stands, which is what the other thirteen want: every one of the eleven
`correction:spectral` estimators is `f(ds, ...)` reading its inputs out of
the Dataset by name, and so are density and conversion.
What `dataset:` costs, recorded because the rows do not show it. All thirteen
return the *same object* they were handed, with their result added to it. So
the row names neither what the method read nor what it wrote, and an observer
diffing the period before against the period after sees one object and no
change. Where a routine plainly reads two variables and writes one, `series:`
roles would make a better record; these do not qualify, because the variables
they read are chosen by name at call time from arguments with defaults.
Why the remaining eleven carry no `run`. Not an omission -- a property of the
functions, established by calling each one rather than by reading it:
* they want a DataArray, and a Dataset is not one: the two
`correction:detrending` rows, `mauder2013` and
`spike_detection_vickers97`. Handed a Dataset they raise AttributeError
(`.to_dataset`, `.data`), TypeError or KeyError, so the `dataset:` role
does not reach them either;
* they take two series rather than a period: the four `correction:time_lag`
rows are `f(move, fix, ...)` and reach for `.values`/`.shift` on each;
* a composite return: the three `correction:axis_rotation` rows take plain
arrays but give back one object carrying u, v, w, theta and phi. A
`passthrough` is one return, and a facade wanting three series cannot
read them out of it without code. `spike_detection_vickers97` has the
same problem one step down: it answers a (data, flags) pair.
Each is a decision per method -- an adapter there, or a signature change here
-- and not a row to fill in.

clone: or, outside a checkout of this repository: git clone https://github.com/pedrohenriquecoimbra/fluxmethods.git, then set FLUXMETHODS_SRC to its fluxmethods/ directory

_comment: layout `tree`: fluxmethods is a package, so its parent goes on sys.path and
its modules are reached as `fluxmethods.<step>.<module>`. A `flat` layout
would import them under bare names, and `signal` would shadow the standard
library module of that name for the duration of the call.
